name: Iceland

observations.reasoning: Sourced on 2026-07-27, transversal pass over the population indicator. Population on 1 January 2025: 389444 inhabitants, recorded as 0.389 million. Eurostat dataset demo_pjan, Population on 1 January by age and sex, read through the dissemination API on 2026-07-27, dataset last updated 2026-07-09. Total population, both sexes, all ages, which is exactly what this indicator's denominator asks for. Read as one table covering every country in the record, so no value here is derived from a neighbour: each is that country's own row. The previous value was an opening estimate produced with no source and no research.

Searched on 2026-07-27, in Icelandic, as part of the transversal venues pass over the smallest countries. Zero, and unlike Liechtenstein or San Marino this one is not for want of puppetry: Iceland has puppetry with premises, and none of it is publicly backed. Two organisations were examined. Brúðuheimar in Borgarnes was a puppet museum and theatre in the old Kaupfélag Borgfirðinga buildings at Englendingavík, founded by the puppet artist Bernd Ogrodnik and the director Hilda Jónsdóttir, and built with 8 000 000 krónur from the Aurora Foundation — a private foundation, which is the whole point: the funding read is not public. Its own domain no longer answers, so it is also not clear the house is still open, and the record says so rather than guessing. Handbendi Brúðuleikhús at Hvammstangi is the live one — original productions, an international residency and the Hvammstangi puppetry festival — and its entry in the Icelandic company register is an ehf., a private limited company, with no public ownership shown. Brúðubíllinn, the puppet van that plays Reykjavík gardens in summer, has no venue at all and is excluded by the denominator on that ground alone. Recorded open rather than verified, because the argument is made from the puppetry side and not from the institutional side: Iceland's publicly funded theatres — the National Theatre, the Reykjavík City Theatre, the Akureyri company — were not read one by one for a puppetry unit, and that is the check that would close this. The previous value was 0.5, an opening estimate produced with no research.

Web check of 2026-07-27. No establishment retained, and no candidate of any kind was identified: the search returned no Icelandic training in puppetry arts, neither degree-granting nor in workshop form. Iceland has a single higher arts school, the Iceland University of the Arts, whose performing arts department was not read at source in this pass. The value of 0 is therefore kept but rests on an absence of results, which is the weakest evidentiary state in this series: finding nothing is not the same as establishing an absence. Upper bound raised from 0 to 1 to carry that weakness. Estimate.

DISPUTED. First value produced as a mean conditioned on artists who actually tour, which drops from the denominator the makers who do not perform. Method error identified: a fee is not a performance. For France the true median probably sits between 10 and 20, over a bimodal distribution. For countries with permanent companies, recomputed from the top: 250 to 400 performances a year, casts of 3 to 5, a company of about twenty, so on the order of 50 to 90. To be redone in full once the denominator is settled.

Find the annual report of at least one organisation in the country.

venues: close the zero from the institutional side. Read Þjóðleikhúsið, Borgarleikhúsið and Menningarfélag Akureyrar for a named puppetry unit; the pass of 2026-07-27 argued only that the two puppetry houses with premises, Brúðuheimar and Handbendi, are private.

venues: establish whether Brúðuheimar in Borgarnes is still open. Its domain no longer answers and no closure was found; a live private house would still not count, but a closed one changes the story.
